question_set_contract.dependency_contract: Exactly two questions use declared prerequisite work knowledge: q01 is direct retrieval and q07 is a mixed derivation and application.
question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: controlled prerequisite retrieval, concept meaning, force and path diagnostics, signed change, complete calculation, then a multi-part derivation with path interpretation

questions.prompt: State what is meant by the work done by a force.
State what is meant by gravitational potential energy. Explain why changing the chosen zero-height level does not change the energy difference between two fixed heights.
A load is raised vertically at constant speed. Resistive forces are negligible. Which pair should replace F and s in W = Fs when deriving its gravitational potential energy increase?

options.C: F = mg and s = total path length

questions.prompt: The same crate is moved without friction from the floor to one platform. Route P is a vertical lift. Route Q is a longer smooth ramp. What can be concluded about the crate's gravitational potential energy changes?

options.A: Route P gives the larger change because its lifting force is larger.
options.B: Route Q gives the larger change because its path is longer.
options.C: Both routes give the same change because the vertical height change is the same.
options.D: The changes cannot be compared without knowing the travel times.

questions.prompt: A 2.0 kg tool is lowered through 3.0 m in a uniform field where g = 9.8 N kg⁻¹. Which value is its change in gravitational potential energy?

A 7.50 kg stage light is raised vertically through 1.80 m at constant speed in a uniform gravitational field. Resistive forces are negligible and g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹. Determine the lifting force, calculate the work done by this force and hence state the increase in gravitational potential energy. Give one independent unit or physical check on your result.

figure.purpose: Assess translation from a steady vertical lift to force, displacement and work
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line diagram of a stage light raised vertically through 1.80 m at constant speed. Label mass 7.50 kg and g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹. Do not draw force values or energy equations.
figure.alt_text: A 7.50 kilogram stage light rises vertically through 1.80 metres at constant speed.

questions.prompt: A 25.0 kg scenery panel moves at constant speed along a smooth inclined rail from a lower platform to an upper platform. The rail is 7.00 m long and the upper platform is 4.20 m vertically above the lower platform. The gravitational field is uniform and g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹.

figure.purpose: Assess the distinction between rail length and vertical height change
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white rail diagram with lower and upper platforms, a 7.00 m sloping rail and a separate vertical bracket of 4.20 m. Show the panel and constant-speed direction but no force values or equations.
figure.alt_text: A scenery panel moves up a 7.00 metre inclined rail to a platform 4.20 metres higher.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Starting from W = Fs, derive ΔE_P = mgΔh for a mass raised vertically at constant speed. State why the lifting force can be replaced by mg.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the increase in gravitational potential energy of the scenery panel.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain why the 4.20 m vertical height, rather than the 7.00 m rail length, appears in your energy calculation.
